already-have.reason: Not already implemented and not contradicted by a recorded owner decision. All five sub-proposals are partially built or tracked by open issues, but the specific deltas the proposal asks for are absent. (1) Wipe-not-halt: the FSBL tripwire halts only (fsbl/src/optbytes.rs:11-43, 80), and the secure world's only runtime option-byte re-check is the mode-production RDP<L2-after-ALL_DONE hard halt plus a SECBOOTADD0 warn (secure/src/main.rs:1240-1290); neither routes to tzic::trigger_intrusion_wipe (secure/src/hw/tzic.rs:228, which is reachable only from TAMP/GTZC tamper and the PIN lockout). The 2026-07-23 owner decision (docs/security/fw-rollback-draft12-candidate-2026-07-21.md:397-405) fixes the FSBL leg as "verify-never-heal, halt on persistent mismatch" and the critical-port doc says "reserve the destructive SE-wipe for confirmed TAMP/GTZC tamper" (trezor-comparison-critical-port-2026-06.md:44); the proposal keeps the FSBL halt and adds a secure-world wipe stage, so it extends rather than contradicts, but the wipe routing is a new owner decision, not a recorded one. (2) OEM pin: shared/src/lockdown.rs:290 OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED = false (fails closed); first_boot Phase A verifies oem_lock_status_raw (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:185-196) but writes no OEMxKEYR; issues #46/#387/#400 (OEM2-ABSENT settler) OPEN. BOOT_LOCK is representable (boot_lock_set, ObField::BootLock) but require_boot_lock = false in both ship profiles (lockdown.rs:343,355) pending the factory sequencing decision in #753 (SECBOOTADD0/SWAP_BANK before BOOT_LOCK, irreversible). (3) HDP1: grep SECHDPCR/HDP1_ACCDIS over secure/src and fsbl/src is empty; verify_ship_profile has no HDP field; #39 (HDP1EN+PEND+ACCDIS at boot-exit), #214, #43 (HDP2 mirror) OPEN; threat-model.md:652 and production-security.md:525-531 document HDP as deferred. (4) BHKLOCK: secure/src/hw/bhk.rs:390 reads BHKLOCK only at load_and_lock and proves the active key via a KAT; no NSC sign handler or crypto.rs path asserts BHKLOCK before SAES/BHK use (grep over secure/src/nsc/*.rs empty). (5) BOR_LEV: lockdown.rs:258-262 is BENCH-CONFIRM and bor_lev() is advisory, not in verify_ship_profile or the confirmed subset; #46 lists BOR_LEV[10:8] as a pin to land.
already-have.corrections: Tracked/partial state the proposal should cite: (a) #39 (HDP1), #214 (BOOT_LOCK+HDP1EN boot-verify), #43 (HDP2/SECWM2 mirror), #46 (register-exact pins incl. OEM key regs OEM1KEYR1/2@0x70/0x74, OEM2KEYR1/2@0x78/0x7C write-only, BOR_LEV[10:8]), #387 (A4b/A4c OEM2 deviation + CubeIDE default-OEM2-password probe), #400 (OEM2-ABSENT bench settler), #38/#753 (BOOT_LOCK; #753 says ordering SECBOOTADD0/SWAP_BANK before BOOT_LOCK is irreversible and require_boot_lock stays false until that factory sequence is decided), #45 (sacrificial BOOT_LOCK dry-run), #366 row tz-1. (b) BOOT_LOCK, WRP2A, SWAP_BANK and ObField::BootLock already exist in verify_ship_profile (lockdown.rs:556-590, landed 2026-09-24) — the delta is only flipping require_boot_lock after #753, not adding the check. (c) The secure-world re-check in main.rs:1240-1290 already hard-halts on RDP regression after journal ALL_DONE under mode-production+rdp2-self-lock; the proposal's delta is to widen that check to the full confirmed set and route it to the wipe path, with the voted/reset-persistent precondition the proposal itself names. Note the halt-sink critique in #835 (halts that burn availability) and the #707/#712 BHK-recoverability thread when choosing BKERASE as the wipe primitive: on a sealed unit a BHK erase makes the SE050 half permanently unrecoverable, which is the intended effect of a wipe but must be stated as a design consequence. (d) The 'OEM1KEYR/OEM2KEYR = 0xFFFFFFFF before OPTSTRT' idiom has no repo precedent and the registers are write-only (read 0 per #46), so it cannot be verified by read-back — only via the OEMxLOCK status bits once #46 pins them. (e) The 2026-07-23 owner decision binds the FSBL leg to halt-only and write-free; the proposal already respects this. (f) Could not check: whether the user holds a separate unrecorded position on wipe-vs-halt for option-byte mismatch; the HDP1 range/SECWM prefix constraint and the OEM-key semantics against RM0456 (not re-derived here).

vendor-claim.reason: The Trezor precedent is substantially true and 'parity' is the right novelty label for sub-items (1),(2),(3),(5): Trezor's U5 boardloader does an exact-equality option-byte compare, force-rewrites in a do/while loop, clears OEM1/OEM2 keys to 0xFFFFFFFF and `ensure`s FLASH->NSSR OEMxLOCK clear, sets BOOT_LOCK in SECBOOTADD0R, includes BOR_LEV in the OPTR compare, enables HDP1 in SECWM1R2, engages HDP1/2_ACCDIS via secret_disable_access, and locks BHK via TAMP_SECCFGR.BHKLOCK; on mismatch the boardloader calls secret_safety_erase (BHK regenerate). The repo_evidence lines all check out, and issues #39/#46/#387 are OPEN. The claim is incomplete rather than false: the wipe-on-mismatch lives in boardloader/main.c (not option_bytes.c), sub-item (4) (assert BHKLOCK before every sign) has NO Trezor precedent (Trezor only reads BHKLOCK to reboot on double-load), Trezor's HDP1 hides the SECRET sector (pages 0..1) not its boardloader code (so proposal (3)'s target differs in purpose from the precedent), the two non-Trezor sources do not support the quoted rationale wording, and — materially — the on-box ST SVD shows PQSigner's OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK bit guess (26/27) is wrong (bits 18/19 of FLASH_NSSR), which strengthens item (2)'s pin requirement.
vendor-claim.corrections: (A) Precedent location/order. The erase-on-mismatch is in /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware/core/embed/projects/boardloader/main.c:325-336, not option_bytes.c: `if (sectrue != option_bytes_configure()) { #ifdef USE_SECRET secret_safety_erase(); #else erase_storage #endif; return 0; }`. option_bytes_configure (option_bytes.c:252-264) REPAIRS first (do { flash_set_option_bytes(); } while (!check)) then calls option_bytes_check_oem_keys and returns secfalse; the boardloader then erases. secret_safety_erase = secret_init + secret_bhk_regenerate (secret.c:655-658; :419-424), i.e. erase the BHK flash record and write a fresh random one — it is NOT a TAMP BKERASE. The check runs every boot in the first (write-capable) stage; PQSigner's adaptation (FSBL halts, secure world wipes) is a necessary deviation, not parity. (B) Sub-item (4) has no Trezor precedent: secret_bhk_locked (secret.c:182-185) is called only from secret_bhk_load (:393-396, reboot_device if ALREADY locked) and secret_reset (:593-596); `grep -rn secret_bhk_locked core/` finds no caller outside secret.c; the kernel asserts only OEM keys at start (kernel/main.c:179-181 under USE_OEM_KEYS_CHECK, enabled per model in core/embed/models/build.rs:276,296,318,337). Novelty for (4) alone is 'beyond' Trezor, not parity. BHKLOCK is set in the BOOTLOADER stage via secret_prepare_fw (bootloader/main.c:430 → secret.c:620-621), before firmware. (C) HDP target differs. Trezor: HDP_AREA_1_PAGE_END = SECRET_SECTOR_END (option_bytes.c:68-69), T3T1 memory.h:29-30 SECRET_SECTOR 0x0..0x1; boardloader lives at 0x0C004000 pages 2..7 (memory.h:38,41) and is WRP-protected (option_bytes.c:33-35) but NOT hidden. Trezor hides SECRETS from later stages; proposal (3) hides the FSBL CODE (a reproducible, public build) — the precedent's security purpose does not transfer, and the risks field already concedes pages 123-127 cannot be covered. Trezor engages ACCDIS in the bootloader (secret.c:650 via :620), not 'the secure world after measured_boot'. (D) OEM-lock bits: ST SVD on box (/home/nicola/STMicroelectronics/STM32Cube/STM32CubeProgrammer/SVD/STM32U585.svd:6322,6409-6421) gives FLASH_NSSR (offset 0x20) OEM1LOCK=bit 18, OEM2LOCK=bit 19. PQSigner's BENCH-CONFIRM constants `OEM1LOCK = 1<<26` / `OEM2LOCK = 1<<27` (shared/src/lockdown.rs:287-288) are WRONG (those are reserved bits → constant-0 → would pass vacuously were the mask pinned); the register read at secure/src/hw/flash.rs:482 (`FLASH_NS + 0x20`) is RIGHT. Trezor agrees: FLASH->NSSR & FLASH_NSSR_OEM1LOCK (option_bytes.c:248-249); 0xFFFFFFFF-clears-the-lock semantics stated at option_bytes.c:213-218. Pins for other fields match PQSigner: SECWM1R2 HDP1EN bit 31 / HDP1_PEND [22:16] (svd:7637-7648), SECHDPCR offset 0xC0 HDP1_ACCDIS bit 0 (svd:9870-9880), TAMP_SECCFGR BHKLOCK bit 30 (svd:157285-157289; bhk.rs const 1<<30), BOR_LEV [10:8] (svd:7105-7109; lockdown.rs:261-262), SECBOOTADD0R BOOT_LOCK bit 0 (svd:7579-7583). (E) Non-Trezor sources: the Ledger Donjon RP2350 post does not contain 'a software-write lock is not a fault-resistant lock' nor any 'detection must be followed by secret destruction' statement; it shows laser FI setting DEBUGEN despite DEBUGEN_LOCK and calls periodic check-and-reset 'best-effort runtime mitigations' that 'do not prevent the pre-firmware secret read'. The Cypherock keylabs.pdf (KeyLabs 2022 audit response, STM32L4+ATECC608A) only supports the threat ('glitches on chips running at RDP2 ... known to induce RDP1 behavior') and recommends PCROP; it says nothing about option-byte check-and-wipe, OEM keys, HDP or BHK. Ledger has no comparable MCU precedent: Ledger states its STM32 MCU 'does not handle any sensitive data'; no published option-byte posture. (F) Repo detail: `handle_fault` does not exist in secure/src/fi.rs (public fns: wait_random, check_true, check_true_into_sentinel, read_volatile_voted, zeroize_barrier, scrub_sentinel_register); the wipe sink is `hw::tzic::trigger_intrusion_wipe` (secure/src/hw/tzic.rs:228, `unsafe fn -> !`, exception-context precondition per tamp.rs:106), gated by `tzic-wipe`/`tamp-wipe`. No secure-world option-byte re-check exists today outside first_boot Phase A (only first_boot/mod.rs and hw/flash.rs reference verify_ship_profile/verify_confirmed_fields), so proposal (1) requires a new site. Trezor also already asserts BOOT_LOCK (option_bytes.c:86-87) where PQSigner's profiles set require_boot_lock=false (lockdown.rs:343,355), and compares BOR_LEV (WANT_BOR_LEVEL, option_bytes.c:40-47) — supports (5).
